summary:
## Follow-up review

The empty-collection guard on `total()` addresses the prior warning: `if not items: return 0` covers both `[]` and `None`, so callers that pass `None` no longer hit `TypeError` on `sum(...)`.

`first_name()` is unchanged — `user.name.split()[0]` still raises `IndexError` when `name` is empty or whitespace-only. That prior warning stays open; no new findings on this diff.

**Recommendation:** request-changes (open prior warning on `first_name`)

5d977ce4424f3a31: Guard `if not items: return 0` handles both [] and None before sum().
09584834c0aebae2: first_name still does user.name.split()[0] with no empty/whitespace guard.

prior_findings_kept.body: first_name() crashes on an empty name ('' .split()[0] → IndexError). first_name still does user.name.split()[0] with no empty/whitespace guard.
